question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is tied to a spring of spring constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, while the other end of spring is fixed at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi></math>. If the body moves about <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi></math> in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be :

solution.text:
Let the extension in spring be x and the natural length of spring be l.

Here the centrifugal force will stretch the spring.

So, centrifugal force=spring force

kx=ml+xω2⇒12.5x=15l+x25⇒1.5x=l⇒xl=11.5=23

⇒x:l=2:3
